However, later on, IO recorded their statements under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. on State vs Monish@Noor Mohammad on 31 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121139341/

However, when they were examined before the Court, they all have resiled from their earlier statements.

PW-1 Rukshar is mother of the deceased, PW-2 Mohd. Arshad is father of the deceased,
PW-3 Aslam and PW-4 Ashraf who are uncles of deceased.
All of them have resiled from their statements and have not supported the case of the prosecution.
They were cross examined in detailed by Ld. APP but nothing could come out from the cross examination.
PW-6 Nishant Haider and PW-7 Mohd. Aftab are neighbours of deceased.
They have stated that deceased was married to accused Monish @ Noor Mohammad as they were residing in front of his house.
They stated that sometimes they used to hear noise of quarreling between them but they stated that they are not aware about the reasons of the same.
26. Their statements before the Court are very vague.
They have stated that they used to hear voices coming out of quarreling from the house but they could not state any reason for the same.
They did not state that they were told about the reasons for such noise by the deceased.
These are very general allegations and devoid of any detailed events.
27. To convict an accused, the allegations must be specific and detailed one.
Vague or general acquisition lack the substance needed to establish the ingredients of an offence.
Vague and general allegations without specific evidence is not sufficient to convict an accused.

28. Needless to say that the family members are hostile.
TWINKLE by TWINKLE WADHWA WADHWA Date: 2025.01.31 16:21:20 +0530 FIR No.
318/2024 State Vs. Monish @ Noor Mohammad page 8 of 10
The statements of police witnesses are only corroborating the case of prosecution and they cannot form basis for conviction.
Police witnesses who are examined in this case have only deposed about the investigation done by them.
29. The convictions must be based on evidence which is credible, trustworthy and directly links accused to the crime.
When public witnesses become hostile, the primary evidence is weakened or nullified.
Corroborating evidence alone, without strong direct evidence, may not meet the legal threshold of proof beyond reasonable doubt.
30. Corroborating evidence refers to secondary or supportive evidence that confirms and strengthens the primary evidence.

It cannot replace the need of credible and direct evidence,
specially when the primary testimony of a public witness becomes unreliable due to his turning State vs Monish@Noor Mohammad on 31 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121139341/
5 hostile to the prosecution.
31.
The Courts must scrutinize the reasons why witnesses turned hostile and then assess whether corroborating evidence can establish the guilt of accused or nor.
If the corroborating evidence does not conclusively points towards the guilt of accused or only provides circumstantial support, it cannot form basis of conviction.
32. Conviction must be based on reliable and convincing evidence which cannot be entirely infringed from corroborating evidence if the main evidence is unreliable.
TWIN  WADH FIR No. 318/2024 State Vs. Monish @ Noor Mohammad
33. According to Section 101 of Evidence Act, the burden of proof is on prosecution to prove their case, however, the prosecution failed to discharge the said burden.
34. In the circumstances, accused namely Monish @ Noor Mohammad is hereby acquitted for the charged offences.
Conclusion:-
35. In the circumstances, in view of above discussion, the accused is hereby acquitted for the charged offences i.e. Section 498-A/304-B of IPC.
